title: List local Time Machine snapshots that take up System Data space
summary: Time Machine can keep local snapshots of your startup disk, and they can make the System Data category in Storage settings large. This read-only check lists these snapshots so you can see whether they are the cause.

aliases.text: mac system data taking space time machine
show time machine snapshots on mac
системные данные на маке занимают много места
system data на mac много места

steps.explain: Show how full the startup disk is. Note the Used and Avail columns of the row whose last column is /, to compare with the System Data size shown in Storage settings later.
steps.expect: A table with Size, Used and Avail columns; the row ending in / is the startup disk.

steps.explain: List the local Time Machine snapshots stored on the startup disk. Each line is one snapshot; the date in its name shows when it was taken. This command shows names and dates only, not sizes. macOS removes these snapshots by itself when disk space runs low.
steps.expect: Usually a header like 'Snapshots for disk /:' and one line per snapshot, e.g. com.apple.TimeMachine.2026-10-20-101500.local. No lines means none.

alternatives.explain: Show only the creation dates of the local snapshots, one per line, in the form YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS.
alternatives.expect: One date per line, such as 2026-10-20-101500. An empty result means there are no local snapshots.

warnings: This card only lists snapshots. Do not delete them with this card; deleting Time Machine snapshots is a separate task and should be done only after you understand what they are.

source.title: tmutil manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
